title: Brain and blood extraction for immunostaining, protein, and RNA measurements after long-term two photon imaging in mice﻿.
protocol: Euthanize mice with a lethal injection of pentobarbital (i.p., 10 mg/kg).
Scruff the mouse to hang straight vertically.
Insert a 22-25G needle with a 3 mL syringe just under the ribs at the body centerline.
Withdraw the syringe plunger gently until blood starts to come out.
Move the syringe slightly upwards or downwards if blood doesn’t come out initially.
Extract a volume of 1-2 mL of blood via cardiac puncture.
Transfer the extracted blood rapidly to a vacutainer blood collection tube with EDTA.
If the blood will be used for RNA extraction, apply three parts of Trizol LS per one part of blood immediately after collection.
Process the blood sample immediately or snap freeze it for later processing.
Place the mouse on its back on a grate sitting on top of the rectangular bucket and tape the forelimbs and hindlimbs firmly to the grate.
Perform a cut from below the ribs to the upper chest in order to expose the chest cavity.
Attach hemostats to the ribs and retract in order to fully expose the heart.
Insert a 21G needle attached to a perfusion pump containing 1X PBS into the left ventricle, and then perform a small cut in the right atrium.
Start to pump 1X PBS to the mouse until the fluid runs clear out of the cut in the right atrium.
Carefully remove the cranial window with forceps.
Decapitate with scissors.
Cut the muscles of the neck and the skin covering the cranium.
Insert scissors through the foramen magnum.
Gently cut the cranial bone up to the rostral side.
Remove lateral bone flaps using forceps.
Expose the brain completely.
Slide curved narrow forceps under the brain and tilt it upward carefully.
Loosen the brain sufficiently with forceps.
Slide the brain out of the cranium and place it in a clean petri dish sitting in an ice bath.
Wash the brain with ice-cold 1X PBS to remove hairs or debris.
Section the brain along the sagittal axis using a clean razor blade.
Separate the cortex from the hippocampus carefully.
Immerse one half of the brain for immunostaining in a tube containing 4% PFA.
Fix the brain overnight at 4°C.
Transfer the fixed brain to a solution containing 30% sucrose after 24 hours.
Snap-freeze the other half or remaining brain sections in liquid nitrogen if desired.
Process the snap-frozen brain for RNA or protein extraction immediately.
For RNA analysis, prepare a tube containing Trizol or lysis buffer with an RNAase inhibitor.
Prepare extraction buffer in a 50 mL conical tube containing 1 mM AESBF and 1 tablet of cOmplete.
Dilute the mixture 1:25 with 1X PBS to make the protein extraction buffer.
Place half brain inside a clean Dounce homogenizer.
Homogenize the brain with 500 uL of extraction buffer using small strokes.
Transfer the homogenized tissue to an Eppendorf tube and keep on ice.
Wash the homogenizer with MilliQ water between samples.
Sonicate tubes in water for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the sample at 14000 rpm (table top centrifuge) for 30 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube.
Store the pellet if further processing is desired.
Proceed with preferred protocol for protein measurement.
Clean all surfaces with RNAzap if performing RNA extraction.
Process samples as quickly as possible for RNA extraction.
Extract the brain from the sucrose solution.
Place the brain in a petri dish.
Position the brain in a coronal or sagittal position inside the metallic cryotome holder with OCT compound as an adhesive.
Let the brain freeze inside the cryotome.
Prepare six tubes for serial sections or label tubes accordingly for regions of interest.
Fill prepared tubes with 1.7 mL of cryoprotection solution.
Mix 150 g of sucrose, 200 mL of 1X PBS, and 150 mL of ethylene glycol to prepare cryoprotection solution.
Complete the final volume of the cryoprotection solution to 500 mL with 1X PBS.
Position the metallic holder into the cryotome.
Trim the OCT adhesive until the brain appears.
Slice the brain with a thickness of 30 µm.
Submerge each slice in PBS and store them alternately in different tubes.
Take one tube stored at 4°C, place the brain slices on a petri dish with 1X PBS.
Mount the slices on a glass slide with a brush.
Draw a rectangle with liquid blocking marker to prevent leakage of solutions.
Wash slices 6 times with PBS for 5 minutes each.
Prepare a blocking solution by adding 250 µL of goat serum, 50 µL of 10% Triton X, and complete to a 5 mL volume using 1X PBS.
Block slides for 30 min with the prepared blocking solution.
Aspirate the blocking solution.
Apply primary antibody (1:500 dilution) in blocking solution.
Incubate overnight at 4°C with a wet paper towel to avoid desiccation.
Aspirate the primary antibody.
Wash slides three times for 5 minutes each with 1X PBS.
Apply secondary antibody at a 1:500 dilution in blocking solution.
Incubate for 2 hours at room temperature in a light-shielded area with a wet paper towel to avoid desiccation.
Aspirate the secondary antibody.
Wash slides three times with 1X PBS.
Apply DAPI or other water-soluble counterstains, if desired.
If labeling amyloid plaques is required, apply Methoxy-X04 diluted at 1:250 in 1X PBS and incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Wash slides twice with 80% ethanol.
Allow slides to thoroughly dry before mounting.
Mount the slides using a preferred medium (recommended: Prolong Gold).
